2x2 matrix stored as two column vectors x and y. Used internally for orientation/axis transforms.
2D transform composed of translation p and rotation r. Used to transform shapes, especially c2Poly, between local and world space. Passing NULL to APIs means identity transform.
2D halfspace/plane with unit normal n and offset d. Used internally for SAT and clipping.
Circle shape defined by center p and radius r. Supported by all collision, ray, manifold, GJK, TOI, and inflate APIs.
Axis-aligned bounding box defined by min and max corners.
Capsule shape defined by segment endpoints a and b and radius r.
Convex polygon with up to C2_MAX_POLYGON_VERTS vertices. verts are CCW; norms are outward face normals. Often used with an optional c2x transform.
Ray defined by origin p, unit direction d, and parametric length t. Many raycast APIs expect d normalized.
Raycast hit information: parametric time t along the ray and contact normal n at impact.
Contact manifold describing up to two contact points, their penetration depths, and the contact normal pointing from shape A to shape B. Populated by Manifold APIs.
Enumeration of supported shape types for generic APIs (c2Collided, c2Collide, c2CastRay, c2GJK, c2TOI, c2Inflate).
Optional cache for c2GJK to warm-start the simplex between calls, improving convergence in temporally coherent cases. Advanced use only.
Result of a time-of-impact query from c2TOI, including hit flag, normalized time, contact normal and point, and iteration count.

	int repeatx;                         // Repeat image in the X direction

RGBA color (8 bits per channel). Used for pixels and palette entries.

A layer definition: visibility/flags, type (normal/group), hierarchy (parent), name, opacity, and user data.
A cel: pixel data for one layer in a particular frame, with position, size, opacity, optional link to another frame, and optional extra precise bounds.
Timeline tag naming a frame range, loop direction, repeat count, and UI color; may carry user data.
A named slice region, optionally with 9-slice center and pivot. May appear per-frame and carry user data.
One palette entry: color plus optional name.
Palette containing up to CUTE_ASEPRITE_MAX_PALETTE_ENTRIES colors.
Optional user data attached to various objects: a color and/or a text string. Flags indicate presence.
Extra cel information with fixed-point precise bounds/position when present.
Color profile metadata: none, sRGB, or embedded ICC with optional fixed gamma. The ICC data buffer is owned by ase_t.
Fixed-point value stored as two 16-bit parts (format specific to Aseprite; exact scaling not documented here).
Bitmask flags describing layer state (visibility, editability, background, etc.).
Layer type: normal or group.
Animation playback direction used by tags: forward, backward, or ping-pong. Note: 'BACKWORDS' appears to be a typo in the source.
Color profile type enumeration for ase_color_profile_t.
Document color mode: RGBA, grayscale, or indexed palette.

Descriptor used to register entries from a premade atlas. Maps a global image_id to UVs within a provided atlas texture and its source w/h.

functions.description: Boolean overlap test between two circles. Returns 1 if the distance between centers is less than the sum of radii; otherwise 0. Fast yes/no, no contact data.
requirements: A and B are valid c2Circle values; radii should be non-negative.
Function is pure and does not modify inputs.
Return value: 1 indicates intersection, 0 indicates no intersection.

functions.name: c2CircletoAABB
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2CircletoAABB(c2Circle A, c2AABB B);
functions.description: Boolean overlap test between a circle and an axis-aligned bounding box (AABB). Returns 1 if the circle intersects the AABB; otherwise 0.
requirements: A is a valid c2Circle (radius non-negative).
B is a valid c2AABB with min <= max on both axes.
Return value: 1 indicates intersection, 0 indicates no intersection.

functions.name: c2CircletoCapsule
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2CircletoCapsule(c2Circle A, c2Capsule B);
functions.description: Boolean overlap test between a circle and a capsule (segment with radius). Returns 1 if intersecting; otherwise 0.
requirements: A is a valid c2Circle (radius non-negative).
B is a valid c2Capsule (radius non-negative).
Return value: 1 indicates intersection, 0 indicates no intersection.

functions.name: c2AABBtoAABB
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2AABBtoAABB(c2AABB A, c2AABB B);
functions.description: Boolean overlap test between two AABBs. Returns 1 if they overlap; otherwise 0.
requirements: A and B are valid c2AABB with min <= max on both axes.
Return value: 1 indicates intersection, 0 indicates no intersection.

functions.name: c2AABBtoCapsule
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2AABBtoCapsule(c2AABB A, c2Capsule B);
functions.description: Boolean overlap test between an AABB and a capsule. Returns 1 if intersecting; otherwise 0. Internally uses GJK.
requirements: A is a valid c2AABB with min <= max on both axes.
B is a valid c2Capsule with non-negative radius.
Return value: 1 indicates intersection, 0 indicates no intersection.
For numeric robustness, keep shape sizes reasonable (the library warns GJK is sensitive to very large scales).

functions.name: c2CapsuletoCapsule
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2CapsuletoCapsule(c2Capsule A, c2Capsule B);
functions.description: Boolean overlap test between two capsules. Returns 1 if intersecting; otherwise 0. Internally uses GJK.
requirements: A and B are valid c2Capsule with non-negative radii.
Return value: 1 indicates intersection, 0 indicates no intersection.
For numeric robustness, keep shape sizes reasonable (GJK sensitive to large scales).

functions.name: c2CircletoPoly
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2CircletoPoly(c2Circle A, const c2Poly* B, const c2x* bx);
functions.description: Boolean overlap test between a circle and a convex polygon. Returns 1 if intersecting; otherwise 0. Optional transform bx applies to the polygon.
requirements: B must be non-NULL and point to a valid convex c2Poly (count in [0, C2_MAX_POLYGON_VERTS], verts/norms valid).
bx may be NULL (treated as identity); otherwise must point to a valid c2x.
A is a valid c2Circle with non-negative radius.
Return value: 1 indicates intersection, 0 indicates no intersection.
For numeric robustness, prefer moderate shape scales (GJK sensitive to large scales).

functions.name: c2AABBtoPoly
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2AABBtoPoly(c2AABB A, const c2Poly* B, const c2x* bx);
functions.description: Boolean overlap test between an AABB and a convex polygon. Returns 1 if intersecting; otherwise 0. Optional transform bx applies to the polygon.
requirements: B must be non-NULL and point to a valid convex c2Poly (count and verts/norms valid).
bx may be NULL (identity) or point to a valid c2x.
A is a valid c2AABB with min <= max.
Return value: 1 indicates intersection, 0 indicates no intersection.
Maintain reasonable numeric scales for stable GJK.

functions.name: c2CapsuletoPoly
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2CapsuletoPoly(c2Capsule A, const c2Poly* B, const c2x* bx);
functions.description: Boolean overlap test between a capsule and a convex polygon. Returns 1 if intersecting; otherwise 0. Optional transform bx applies to the polygon.
requirements: B must be non-NULL and point to a valid convex c2Poly.
bx may be NULL (identity) or a valid c2x.
A is a valid c2Capsule with non-negative radius.
Return value: 1 indicates intersection, 0 indicates no intersection.
Maintain reasonable numeric scales for stable GJK.

functions.name: c2PolytoPoly
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2PolytoPoly(const c2Poly* A, const c2x* ax, const c2Poly* B, const c2x* bx);
functions.description: Boolean overlap test between two convex polygons. Returns 1 if intersecting; otherwise 0. Optional transforms ax/bx apply to A/B respectively.
requirements: A and B must be non-NULL and valid convex c2Poly instances (count and verts/norms valid, count <= C2_MAX_POLYGON_VERTS).
ax and bx may be NULL (identity) or valid pointers to c2x transforms.
Return value: 1 indicates intersection, 0 indicates no intersection.
Maintain reasonable numeric scales for stable GJK.

functions.name: c2RaytoCircle
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2RaytoCircle(c2Ray A, c2Circle B, c2Raycast* out);
functions.description: Ray cast against a circle. On hit, writes time of impact (t) and surface normal at impact to out and returns 1; otherwise returns 0.
requirements: out must be a non-NULL pointer to c2Raycast to receive results; contents are meaningful only if the function returns 1.
A.d (ray direction) is recommended to be normalized; A.t specifies the ray length along A.d.
B is a valid c2Circle with non-negative radius.
Return value: 1 indicates a hit within [0, A.t], 0 indicates no hit.

functions.name: c2RaytoAABB
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2RaytoAABB(c2Ray A, c2AABB B, c2Raycast* out);
functions.description: Ray cast against an AABB. On hit, writes time of impact and the box face normal at impact to out and returns 1; otherwise 0.
requirements: out must be non-NULL to receive results; valid only if return is 1.
A.d is recommended to be normalized; A.t is the ray length.
B must be a valid AABB with min <= max.
Return value: 1 indicates hit, 0 indicates no hit.

functions.name: c2RaytoCapsule
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2RaytoCapsule(c2Ray A, c2Capsule B, c2Raycast* out);
functions.description: Ray cast against a capsule. On hit, writes time of impact and surface normal at impact to out and returns 1; otherwise 0.
requirements: out must be non-NULL to receive results; only valid if return is 1.
A.d is recommended to be normalized; A.t is the ray length.
B is a valid c2Capsule with non-negative radius.
Return value: 1 indicates hit, 0 indicates no hit.

functions.name: c2RaytoPoly
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2RaytoPoly(c2Ray A, const c2Poly* B, const c2x* bx_ptr, c2Raycast* out);
functions.description: Ray cast against a convex polygon. Optional transform bx_ptr applies to the polygon. On hit, fills out with the time of impact and the world-space normal of the polygon face hit.
requirements: B must be non-NULL and a valid convex c2Poly.
bx_ptr may be NULL (identity) or a valid c2x transform.
out must be non-NULL; values valid only if return is 1.
A.d is recommended to be normalized; A.t is the ray length.
Return value: 1 on hit, 0 on miss.

functions.name: c2CircletoCircleManifold
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API void c2CircletoCircleManifold(c2Circle A, c2Circle B, c2Manifold* m);
functions.description: Generates a contact manifold for two intersecting circles. If no collision, sets m->count = 0. On collision, fills normal from A to B, penetration depth, and contact point.
requirements: m must be non-NULL and point to a writable c2Manifold.
A and B are valid circles (r >= 0).
On no collision, m->count is set to 0; callers must check m->count before using other fields.

functions.name: c2CircletoAABBManifold
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API void c2CircletoAABBManifold(c2Circle A, c2AABB B, c2Manifold* m);
functions.description: Generates a contact manifold for a circle vs. AABB. If not colliding, sets m->count = 0; otherwise fills one contact with normal, depth, and point.
requirements: m must be non-NULL and writable.
A is a valid circle; B is a valid AABB with min <= max.
Callers must check m->count to see if a collision occurred.

functions.name: c2CircletoCapsuleManifold
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API void c2CircletoCapsuleManifold(c2Circle A, c2Capsule B, c2Manifold* m);
functions.description: Generates a contact manifold for a circle vs. capsule. Sets m->count = 0 if separated; otherwise fills a single contact with normal from A to B, depth, and point.
requirements: m must be non-NULL.
A and B valid shapes (non-negative radii).
Callers must check m->count before using contact data.
Maintain reasonable numeric scales (uses GJK internally for closest points).

functions.name: c2AABBtoAABBManifold
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API void c2AABBtoAABBManifold(c2AABB A, c2AABB B, c2Manifold* m);
functions.description: Generates a contact manifold for two AABBs. On overlap, produces one contact point on A’s surface facing B with normal from A to B and depth; otherwise m->count = 0.
requirements: m must be non-NULL.
A and B are valid AABBs (min <= max).
Check m->count to determine collision.

functions.name: c2AABBtoCapsuleManifold
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API void c2AABBtoCapsuleManifold(c2AABB A, c2Capsule B, c2Manifold* m);
functions.description: Generates a contact manifold for AABB vs. capsule by converting the AABB to a poly and delegating to capsule-vs-poly manifold. Sets m->count = 0 if separated.
requirements: m must be non-NULL.
A valid c2AABB; B valid c2Capsule.
Check m->count before using.
Normal is oriented from A to B as per convention.

functions.name: c2CapsuletoCapsuleManifold
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API void c2CapsuletoCapsuleManifold(c2Capsule A, c2Capsule B, c2Manifold* m);
functions.description: Generates a contact manifold for two capsules. On intersection, produces one contact with normal from A to B, depth, and contact point; otherwise m->count = 0.
requirements: m must be non-NULL.
A and B are valid capsules (r >= 0).
Check m->count to determine if collision occurred.
Maintain reasonable numeric scales (GJK used to find closest points in shallow cases).

functions.name: c2CircletoPolyManifold
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API void c2CircletoPolyManifold(c2Circle A, const c2Poly* B, const c2x* bx, c2Manifold* m);
functions.description: Generates a contact manifold for a circle vs. convex polygon. Uses GJK to determine shallow contacts; if the circle center is inside the polygon, projects to the nearest face. Sets m->count = 0 on no collision.
requirements: m must be non-NULL.
B must be non-NULL and a valid convex c2Poly; bx may be NULL (identity).
A is a valid circle.
Check m->count before using data.
Maintain reasonable numeric scales for stability.

functions.name: c2AABBtoPolyManifold
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API void c2AABBtoPolyManifold(c2AABB A, const c2Poly* B, const c2x* bx, c2Manifold* m);
functions.description: Generates a contact manifold for AABB vs. convex polygon by forming a 4-vertex poly from the AABB and calling poly-vs-poly manifold. Sets m->count = 0 if separated.
requirements: m must be non-NULL.
B must be non-NULL and a valid convex c2Poly; bx may be NULL (identity).
A must be a valid AABB.
Check m->count before using data.

functions.name: c2CapsuletoPolyManifold
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API void c2CapsuletoPolyManifold(c2Capsule A, const c2Poly* B, const c2x* bx, c2Manifold* m);
functions.description: Generates a contact manifold for capsule vs. convex polygon. Handles deep cases with segment-vs-poly clipping and shallow cases via GJK. Sets m->count = 0 if separated.
requirements: m must be non-NULL.
B must be non-NULL and a valid convex c2Poly; bx may be NULL (identity).
A must be a valid c2Capsule (non-negative radius).
Check m->count before using results.
Maintain reasonable numeric scales (uses GJK for shallow cases).

functions.name: c2PolytoPolyManifold
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API void c2PolytoPolyManifold(const c2Poly* A, const c2x* ax, const c2Poly* B, const c2x* bx, c2Manifold* m);
functions.description: Generates a contact manifold for two convex polygons using Separating Axis Theorem and clipping (reference/incident faces). Sets m->count = 0 if separated.
requirements: m must be non-NULL.
A and B must be non-NULL, valid convex c2Poly with count <= C2_MAX_POLYGON_VERTS.
ax and bx may be NULL (identity) or valid c2x transforms.
Check m->count before using contact data.

functions.name: c2GJK
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API float c2GJK(const void* A, C2_TYPE typeA, const c2x* ax_ptr, const void* B, C2_TYPE typeB, const c2x* bx_ptr, c2v* outA, c2v* outB, int use_radius, int* iterations, c2GJKCache* cache);
functions.description: Advanced function running the GJK algorithm to compute the closest points between two shapes and their distance. Returns the distance. If outA/outB are non-NULL, they are set to the witness points. Optional transforms ax_ptr/bx_ptr are local-to-world transforms. If use_radius is non-zero, circle/capsule radii are applied; otherwise spheres/segments are treated as points/lines. iterations and cache are optional for diagnostics and warm-starting.
requirements: A and B must point to shapes matching typeA and typeB respectively; valid types are C2_TYPE_CIRCLE, C2_TYPE_AABB, C2_TYPE_CAPSULE, C2_TYPE_POLY.
ax_ptr and bx_ptr may be NULL (identity) or point to valid c2x transforms.
outA and outB may be NULL; if non-NULL they must be writable.
iterations may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be writable to receive iteration count.
cache may be NULL; if non-NULL it must point to a c2GJKCache used for warm starting.
For numeric robustness, avoid very large shapes or coordinates; the implementation warns GJK is sensitive to large scales.

functions.name: c2TOI
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API c2TOIResult c2TOI(const void* A, C2_TYPE typeA, const c2x* ax_ptr, c2v vA, const void* B, C2_TYPE typeB, const c2x* bx_ptr, c2v vB, int use_radius);
functions.description: Advanced time-of-impact (sweep) test between two shapes moving linearly without rotation over time [0,1]. Returns a c2TOIResult containing hit flag, time of impact, contact normal, point of contact, and iteration count. Optional transforms ax_ptr/bx_ptr transform shapes to world space. If use_radius is non-zero, circle/capsule radii are considered; otherwise capsules become line segments and circles points.
requirements: A and B must point to shapes matching typeA and typeB.
ax_ptr and bx_ptr may be NULL (identity) or valid c2x transforms.
vA and vB represent the total movement from time 0 to 1 (no rotation supported).
The function assumes no rotation during the sweep.
For stable results, consider small skin factors or inflation/deflation strategies as recommended in the documentation.
Maintain reasonable numeric scales; algorithm uses GJK-raycast internally.

functions.name: c2Inflate
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API void c2Inflate(void* shape, C2_TYPE type, float skin_factor);
functions.description: Inflates (grows) or deflates (shrinks) a shape by a skin factor. For circles/capsules, adjusts radius; for AABBs, expands/deflates min/max; for polys, computes an inflated/deflated poly via dual/hull operations.
requirements: shape must be a non-NULL pointer to a shape instance matching the provided type.
type must be one of C2_TYPE_CIRCLE, C2_TYPE_AABB, C2_TYPE_CAPSULE, C2_TYPE_POLY.
skin_factor can be positive (inflate) or negative (deflate).

Documentation warns: sharp polygon corners can move dramatically when inflating; deflating very small shapes can invert planes and break convexity. Choose an appropriately small skin factor (e.g., 1.0e-6).

functions.name: c2Hull
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2Hull(c2v* verts, int count);
functions.description: Computes the 2D convex hull in-place on the provided point set. Returns the number of vertices in the hull. If fewer than two vertices are provided, it does nothing. If more than C2_MAX_POLYGON_VERTS are provided, extras are ignored.
requirements: verts must be a non-NULL writable array with at least 'count' elements.
count >= 0; fewer than 2 points yields no meaningful hull (function returns 0).
Only the first C2_MAX_POLYGON_VERTS points are considered; extra points are ignored.
The function writes the hull vertices back into the verts array and returns the hull count.

functions.name: c2Norms
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API void c2Norms(c2v* verts, c2v* norms, int count);
functions.description: Computes outward unit edge normals for a polygon defined by verts[0..count-1] (assumed CCW). Writes one normal per edge into norms[0..count-1].
requirements: verts must be a non-NULL array of at least 'count' vertices representing a polygon (ideally convex, CCW).
norms must be a non-NULL writable array with at least 'count' entries.
count >= 0; the function accesses indices [0..count-1] and wraps the last edge to 0.

functions.name: c2MakePoly
functions.description: Runs convex hull generation (c2Hull) on p->verts using p->count, then computes normals (c2Norms) to finalize a convex c2Poly.
requirements: p must be non-NULL.
Before calling, p->count must be set and p->verts must contain at least p->count points.
On return, p->count is updated to the hull count and p->norms are filled.
C2_MAX_POLYGON_VERTS caps the number of vertices in the resulting polygon.

functions.name: c2Collided
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2Collided(const void* A, const c2x* ax, C2_TYPE typeA, const void* B, const c2x* bx, C2_TYPE typeB);
functions.description: Generic boolean collision test between two shapes of potentially different types. Dispatches to the corresponding c2***to*** function. For polys, optional transforms ax/bx are applied; for other shapes transforms are ignored.
requirements: A and B must point to shape instances matching typeA and typeB.
typeA/typeB must be valid C2_TYPE values (not C2_TYPE_NONE).
ax/bx may be NULL (identity) or valid transforms; they are used only for polygons.
Return value: 1 indicates intersection, 0 indicates no intersection.

functions.name: c2Collide
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API void c2Collide(const void* A, const c2x* ax, C2_TYPE typeA, const void* B, const c2x* bx, C2_TYPE typeB, c2Manifold* m);
functions.description: Generic manifold generation between two shapes of potentially different types. Dispatches to the corresponding c2***to***Manifold function. Normal is oriented from A to B (the function adjusts orientation where necessary).
requirements: A and B must point to shape instances matching typeA and typeB.
typeA/typeB must be valid C2_TYPE values.
ax/bx may be NULL (identity) or valid transforms; used for polygons.
m must be non-NULL and writable.
Callers must check m->count after the call to determine collision.

functions.name: c2CastRay
functions.signature: CUTE_C2_API int c2CastRay(c2Ray A, const void* B, const c2x* bx, C2_TYPE typeB, c2Raycast* out);
functions.description: Generic ray cast against a single shape. Dispatches to c2Rayto*** based on typeB. Optional transform bx applies to polygons; ignored for other shapes. Returns 1 on hit and fills out; otherwise 0.
requirements: B must point to a shape instance matching typeB.
typeB must be a valid C2_TYPE.
bx may be NULL (identity) or valid; only used for polygons.
out must be non-NULL to receive results; valid only if return is 1.
A.d is recommended to be normalized; A.t is the ray length.

functions.name: cn_endpoint_init
functions.signature: int cn_endpoint_init(cn_endpoint_t* endpoint, const char* address_and_port_string);
functions.description: Parses an IPv4 or IPv6 address string (optionally with port) and initializes a cn_endpoint_t. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure. Expected usage: parse strings like "127.0.0.1:5000", "[::1]:5000", or address without port; for IPv6 with port, use bracketed form.
requirements: endpoint must be non-null.
address_and_port_string must be a null-terminated C string representing a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address; port is optional for IPv4 (e.g. ":5000") and for IPv6 must be specified as "[addr]:port".
On success returns 0; on invalid address returns -1.
The function modifies its local copy of the input string (internally) but does not modify the caller’s input buffer.

functions.name: cn_endpoint_to_string
functions.signature: void cn_endpoint_to_string(cn_endpoint_t endpoint, char* buffer, int buffer_size);
functions.description: Formats an endpoint into a human-readable IP (and optional port) string into buffer. IPv6 addresses are bracketed when a port is present. Expected usage: after obtaining an endpoint, convert it to string for logging.
requirements: buffer must be non-null.
buffer_size must be >= 0 and large enough to hold the output; CN_ENDPOINT_STRING_MAX_LENGTH (INET6_ADDRSTRLEN) is recommended.
Output may be truncated if buffer_size is too small.

functions.name: cn_endpoint_equals
functions.description: Compares two endpoints for equality, including address type, address value, and port. Returns 1 if equal, 0 otherwise.
requirements: None beyond providing initialized endpoints.

functions.name: cn_crypto_generate_key
functions.description: Generates a cryptographically secure symmetric key for encryption (32 bytes). Internally ensures crypto is initialized. Expected usage: create per-connection or per-token keys.
requirements: No inputs. Returns a fully initialized key.
Relies on platform crypto initialization internally; no explicit caller init required.

functions.name: cn_crypto_random_bytes
functions.description: Fills the given buffer with cryptographically secure random bytes. Slower but strong randomness. Expected usage: generate nonces, test data, etc.
requirements: data must be non-null.
byte_count must be >= 0 and should not exceed available buffer size.

functions.name: cn_crypto_sign_keygen
functions.description: Generates a public/secret keypair used by the library for signing (connect token authentication). Expected usage: run on the server/web service to provision keys.
requirements: public_key and secret_key must be non-null pointers to output buffers of sizes 32 and 64 bytes respectively (as per their types).
Keys should be stored securely; secret key must remain private.

functions.name: cn_generate_connect_token
functions.signature: cn_result_t cn_generate_connect_token(uint64_t application_id, uint64_t creation_timestamp, const cn_crypto_key_t* client_to_server_key, const cn_crypto_key_t* server_to_client_key, uint64_t expiration_timestamp, uint32_t handshake_timeout, int address_count, const char** address_list, uint64_t client_id, const uint8_t* user_data, const cn_crypto_sign_secret_t* shared_secret_key, uint8_t* token_ptr_out);
functions.description: Builds a cryptographically protected connect token for clients to authenticate and connect to servers. The token contains public parameters (server endpoints, timeouts) and a secret section (keys, client id, optional user data) encrypted and signed. Expected usage: on a secure web service after authenticating a player, generate a token and deliver to the client.
requirements: application_id must match the application_id used by cn_client_create and cn_server_create.
creation_timestamp must be less than expiration_timestamp (UNIX timestamps).
client_to_server_key and server_to_client_key must be non-null and point to valid 32-byte keys (cn_crypto_generate_key).
handshake_timeout is in seconds.
address_count must be between 1 and 32 inclusive.
address_list must be non-null and contain address_count C strings, each parseable by cn_endpoint_init (e.g., "127.0.0.1:5000", "[::1]:5000").
client_id is a unique identifier for the client.
user_data may be NULL or point to CN_CONNECT_TOKEN_USER_DATA_SIZE (256) bytes; if NULL, user data is zeroed.
shared_secret_key must be non-null; it is the signing/crypto key shared between the web service and game servers (must not be public).
token_ptr_out must point to a writable buffer of size CN_CONNECT_TOKEN_SIZE (1114) bytes.
Returns cn_error_success on success; otherwise cn_error_failure with details.

functions.name: cn_client_create
functions.signature: cn_client_t* cn_client_create(uint16_t port, uint64_t application_id, bool use_ipv6, void* user_allocator_context);
functions.description: Creates a client instance, opening a UDP socket on the given port (or ephemeral if 0) for a specific application_id. Expected usage: allocate once per client; then connect with cn_client_connect and drive with cn_client_update.
requirements: application_id must match the server’s application_id.
If use_ipv6 is true, the platform must have IPv6 support; otherwise creation may fail (library may be compiled without IPv6).
user_allocator_context is optional and may be NULL.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cn_client_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a client and releases resources. Safe to call when disconnected; disconnects if necessary.
requirements: client must be a valid pointer returned by cn_client_create.
After destruction, the pointer must not be used.

functions.name: cn_client_connect
functions.signature: cn_result_t cn_client_connect(cn_client_t* client, const uint8_t* connect_token);
functions.description: Begins the connection process to servers listed in the connect token (tries each in order). Sets internal state and expects periodic cn_client_update calls to perform the handshake and manage timeouts.
requirements: client must be a valid client created by cn_client_create.
connect_token must point to CN_CONNECT_TOKEN_SIZE (1114) bytes produced by cn_generate_connect_token.
After calling, periodically invoke cn_client_update until connected or an error state is reached.
Returns cn_error_success on start; sets state to error if token invalid or later failures occur.

functions.name: cn_client_disconnect
functions.description: Disconnects from the server if connected (sends redundant disconnect packets) and resets client to a disconnected state.
requirements: client must be a valid client pointer.
No-op if already disconnected.

functions.name: cn_client_update
functions.signature: void cn_client_update(cn_client_t* client, double dt, uint64_t current_time);
functions.description: Advances the client’s networking state, processes handshakes, retries, and IO. Call once per game tick after cn_client_connect. current_time is used for token expiration/timeouts.
requirements: client must have been created; typically call only after cn_client_connect.
dt should be the elapsed time in seconds since the last update; must be >= 0.
current_time should be monotonically increasing (UNIX timestamp or similar) to ensure correct timeout/expiration behavior.
Must be called regularly for reliable operation.

functions.name: cn_client_pop_packet
functions.signature: bool cn_client_pop_packet(cn_client_t* client, void** packet, int* size, bool* was_sent_reliably);
functions.description: Retrieves the next received payload packet from the server if available. Returns true and sets packet and size; caller must free the packet with cn_client_free_packet. Optionally reports whether it was sent reliably.
requirements: client must be connected (function returns false if not).
packet and size must be non-null; was_sent_reliably may be NULL.
The returned packet pointer must be freed with cn_client_free_packet when done.
Do not modify or free with other allocators.

functions.name: cn_client_free_packet
functions.description: Frees a packet previously returned by cn_client_pop_packet.
requirements: packet must be a pointer previously returned by cn_client_pop_packet for this client and not yet freed.
Do not pass arbitrary pointers.

functions.name: cn_client_send
functions.signature: cn_result_t cn_client_send(cn_client_t* client, const void* packet, int size, bool send_reliably);
functions.description: Sends a payload packet to the server. Large packets are fragmented and reassembled automatically. If send_reliably is true, the packet is sent reliably-in-order; otherwise it’s fire-and-forget (unreliable).
requirements: client must be connected; otherwise returns an error.
packet must point to valid memory of length size.
size must be > 0; empty packets are not allowed.
Very large packets are supported but may be limited by internal max single-send; the function returns an error if the send queue is full or other resource limits are hit.

When using reliable packets, two-way traffic is required to acknowledge packets; ensure periodic bidirectional sends to avoid stalling (library note: send at least one packet back for every ~16 received).

functions.name: cn_client_state_get
functions.description: Returns the current client state (disconnected, connecting, connected, or error states).
requirements: client must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: cn_client_state_string
functions.description: Returns a static string for a given client state enum value.
requirements: state must be a valid cn_client_state_t value.

functions.name: cn_client_enable_network_simulator
functions.signature: void cn_client_enable_network_simulator(cn_client_t* client, double latency, double jitter, double drop_chance, double duplicate_chance);
functions.description: Enables a client-side network simulator that injects artificial latency, jitter, packet drops, and duplicates for testing.
requirements: latency and jitter are in seconds and should be >= 0.
drop_chance and duplicate_chance are probabilities; expected range is 0.0 to 1.0.
Call after client creation; can be enabled before or after connecting.

functions.name: cn_client_get_packet_loss_estimate
functions.description: Returns the client’s current estimated packet loss (0..1).
requirements: client should be connected and updating; otherwise estimate may be meaningless.

functions.name: cn_client_get_rtt_estimate
functions.description: Returns the current estimated round-trip time in milliseconds.
requirements: Client should be connected and updating for a meaningful estimate.

functions.name: cn_client_get_incoming_kbps_estimate
functions.description: Returns estimated incoming bandwidth in kilobits per second.
requirements: Client should be connected and updating for a meaningful estimate.

functions.name: cn_client_get_outgoing_kbps_estimate
functions.description: Returns estimated outgoing bandwidth in kilobits per second.
requirements: Client should be connected and updating for a meaningful estimate.

functions.name: cn_server_config_defaults
functions.description: Returns a cn_server_config_t initialized with sensible defaults (timeouts, resend rate). Public/secret keys are zero-initialized and must be set by the caller before starting the server.
requirements: Use the returned struct as a starting point; set application_id, public_key, secret_key as appropriate before cn_server_create/cn_server_start.

functions.name: cn_server_create
functions.description: Creates a server object using the supplied configuration. Does not bind or start listening; call cn_server_start afterwards. Expected usage: one server per listening socket.
requirements: config.application_id must match clients.
config.public_key and config.secret_key must be set appropriately (generated via cn_crypto_sign_keygen) to authenticate tokens.
Returns NULL on failure.

functions.name: cn_server_destroy
functions.description: Destroys the server object and releases resources. Calls cn_server_stop if running.
requirements: server must be a valid pointer returned by cn_server_create.
After destruction, the pointer must not be used.

functions.name: cn_server_start
functions.signature: cn_result_t cn_server_start(cn_server_t* server, const char* address_and_port);
functions.description: Starts the server by binding a UDP socket to the provided address and port, initializes internal structures, and begins accepting connections.
requirements: server must be a valid server created by cn_server_create.
address_and_port must be a valid bindable local address (e.g., "[::]:5000" or "0.0.0.0:5000").
Returns cn_error_success on success; cn_error_failure on error (e.g., bind failure).

functions.name: cn_server_stop
functions.description: Stops the server, disconnects clients, frees any queued payload packets, and resets internal state. Preserves simulator settings by re-initializing it.
requirements: server must be valid. Safe to call even if already stopped.

functions.name: cn_server_pop_event
functions.description: Pops the next server event (new connection, disconnect, or payload packet). Returns true if an event was written into event. Payload data must be released with cn_server_free_packet.
requirements: server and event must be non-null.
If event.type == CN_SERVER_EVENT_TYPE_PAYLOAD_PACKET, the data pointer in the event must later be freed via cn_server_free_packet with the correct client index.

functions.name: cn_server_free_packet
functions.signature: void cn_server_free_packet(cn_server_t* server, int client_index, void* data);
functions.description: Frees a payload packet previously delivered via a server event for the specified client.
requirements: data must be a pointer obtained from a CN_SERVER_EVENT_TYPE_PAYLOAD_PACKET event for this server and client_index.
client_index must be a valid, currently connected client at the time of freeing.

functions.name: cn_server_update
functions.signature: void cn_server_update(cn_server_t* server, double dt, uint64_t current_time);
functions.description: Advances server networking, processes incoming data, sends keepalives/challenges, and manages timeouts. Call once per game tick.
requirements: server must be running (after cn_server_start).
dt should be >= 0 seconds and current_time should be monotonic for correct timeout checks.
Call regularly for stable behavior.

functions.name: cn_server_disconnect_client
functions.signature: void cn_server_disconnect_client(cn_server_t* server, int client_index, bool notify_client);
functions.description: Disconnects a connected client by index. Optionally notifies the client (sends redundant disconnect packets).
requirements: client_index must reference a currently connected client.
If notify_client is true, the server will send disconnect packets before removal.

functions.name: cn_server_send
functions.signature: cn_result_t cn_server_send(cn_server_t* server, const void* packet, int size, int client_index, bool send_reliably);
functions.description: Sends a payload packet to a specific connected client. Large payloads are fragmented transparently. send_reliably selects reliable-in-order or unreliable delivery.
requirements: client_index must be a currently connected client.
packet must point to a valid buffer of length size.
size must be > 0; empty packets are not allowed.
Returns cn_error_failure if the packet cannot be queued (e.g., queue full) or other errors occur.

functions.name: cn_server_is_client_connected
functions.description: Returns true if the specified client index is currently connected.
requirements: client_index must be within [0, CN_SERVER_MAX_CLIENTS).

functions.name: cn_server_set_public_ip
functions.signature: void cn_server_set_public_ip(cn_server_t* server, const char* address_and_port);
functions.description: Overrides the server’s public IP matching to use a specified address for validation during token processing. Intended only for testing behind NAT (developer mode); reduces security.
requirements: Use only in development/testing; not recommended for production due to compromised security.
address_and_port must be a valid address string parseable by cn_endpoint_init.

functions.name: cn_server_enable_network_simulator
functions.signature: void cn_server_enable_network_simulator(cn_server_t* server, double latency, double jitter, double drop_chance, double duplicate_chance);
functions.description: Enables a server-side network simulator that injects latency, jitter, drops, and duplicates for testing across all clients.
requirements: latency and jitter are in seconds and should be >= 0.
drop_chance and duplicate_chance are probabilities (expected 0.0..1.0).

functions.name: cn_server_get_packet_loss_estimate
functions.description: Returns the estimated packet loss (0..1) for a connected client.
requirements: client_index must reference a connected client.
Server should be updating for a meaningful estimate.

functions.name: cn_server_get_rtt_estimate
functions.description: Returns the estimated RTT in milliseconds for a connected client.
requirements: client_index must reference a connected client.
Server should be updating for a meaningful estimate.

functions.name: cn_server_get_incoming_kbps_estimate
functions.description: Returns the estimated incoming bandwidth (client->server) in kilobits per second for a connected client.
requirements: client_index must reference a connected client.
Server should be updating for a meaningful estimate.

functions.name: cn_server_get_outgoing_kbps_estimate
functions.description: Returns the estimated outgoing bandwidth (server->client) in kilobits per second for a connected client.
requirements: client_index must reference a connected client.
Server should be updating for a meaningful estimate.

functions.name: cn_is_error
functions.description: Utility to check if a cn_result_t indicates failure (returns true if result.code == CN_ERROR_FAILURE).
requirements: result.details may contain a message on failure; callers should not free it.

functions.name: cn_error_failure
functions.description: Constructs a failure cn_result_t with an error message pointer.
requirements: details may be NULL or a pointer to a constant/lifetime-valid string; the library does not take ownership.

functions.name: cn_error_success
functions.description: Constructs a success cn_result_t (code = CN_ERROR_SUCCESS, details = NULL).
requirements: None.

functions.name: cute_tiled_load_map_from_file
functions.signature: cute_tiled_map_t* cute_tiled_load_map_from_file(const char* path, void* mem_ctx);
functions.description: Loads a Tiled JSON map from a file path into heap-allocated structures and returns the root cute_tiled_map_t. Intended for Tiled-exported JSON maps using CSV (uncompressed) tile data. On parse errors, returns NULL and emits a warning; global error info (cute_tiled_error_reason/line) describe the issue. Use cute_tiled_free_map to free the result.
requirements: path must point to a readable Tiled JSON map file.
The map’s tilelayer data must be CSV (uncompressed). Base64/encoding/compression are not supported.
mem_ctx may be NULL; it’s passed through to the allocator hooks.
On failure this returns NULL and prints a warning (via CUTE_TILED_WARNING). Check the return value before use.
Call cute_tiled_free_map on the returned pointer when done. Do not attempt to free with free/malloc directly.
If the map references external tilesets and they are not embedded, a warning may be printed unless CUTE_TILED_NO_EXTERNAL_TILESET_WARNING is defined.

functions.name: cute_tiled_load_map_from_memory
functions.signature: cute_tiled_map_t* cute_tiled_load_map_from_memory(const void* memory, int size_in_bytes, void* mem_ctx);
functions.description: Parses a Tiled JSON map from an in-memory buffer and returns a heap-allocated cute_tiled_map_t view. The buffer is read-only during parse and does not need to be NUL-terminated. On error, parsing emits a warning and returns NULL. Use cute_tiled_free_map to free the result.
requirements: memory must be non-NULL. Passing NULL triggers a crash via CUTE_TILED_CRASH.
size_in_bytes must be the exact byte size of the JSON buffer (no NUL terminator required).
Buffer contents must be a valid Tiled JSON map and use CSV (uncompressed) tilelayer data; encoding/compression are not supported.
mem_ctx may be NULL; it’s forwarded to the allocator hooks.
On failure returns NULL and prints a warning (global cute_tiled_error_reason/line/file provide context). Check the return value before use.
Call cute_tiled_free_map on the returned pointer when done. Do not double-free or mix allocators.

functions.name: cute_tiled_reverse_layers
functions.description: Reverses the singly-linked list of top-level layers in the map so their order is the reverse of how they were parsed (matching reverse-order from the Tiled editor if desired). Does not recurse into group sublayer order (only reverses the head list).
requirements: map must be a valid map pointer obtained from cute_tiled_load_map_from_file/memory.
Does not allocate or free memory; it mutates the layer list in place.
Safe to call at most once if you need a single reversal; calling multiple times toggles order each time.

functions.name: cute_tiled_free_map
functions.description: Frees all dynamic memory associated with a map previously returned by cute_tiled_load_map_from_file or cute_tiled_load_map_from_memory. After this call, the pointer becomes invalid.
requirements: map must be a pointer previously returned by cute_tiled_load_map_from_file or cute_tiled_load_map_from_memory.
Do not call more than once for the same map (no double-free).
Do not mix with other deallocation methods; this performs internal page and pool cleanup.

functions.name: cute_tiled_load_external_tileset
functions.signature: cute_tiled_tileset_t* cute_tiled_load_external_tileset(const char* path, void* mem_ctx);
functions.description: Loads a Tiled tileset (TSX exported as JSON) from a file path into heap-allocated structures and returns the cute_tiled_tileset_t. Useful when intentionally loading tilesets separately from maps. Use cute_tiled_free_external_tileset to free.
requirements: path must point to a readable Tiled tileset JSON file.
mem_ctx may be NULL; it’s passed to allocator hooks.
On failure returns NULL and prints a warning. Check the return value.
Call cute_tiled_free_external_tileset on the returned tileset when done.

functions.name: cute_tiled_load_external_tileset_from_memory
functions.signature: cute_tiled_tileset_t* cute_tiled_load_external_tileset_from_memory(const void* memory, int size_in_bytes, void* mem_ctx);
functions.description: Parses a Tiled tileset from an in-memory JSON buffer and returns a heap-allocated cute_tiled_tileset_t. The buffer need not be NUL-terminated. Use cute_tiled_free_external_tileset to free.
requirements: memory must be non-NULL and point to a valid Tiled tileset JSON buffer.
size_in_bytes must be the exact size of the buffer in bytes.
mem_ctx may be NULL; it’s forwarded to allocator hooks.
On success, tileset->_internal is set for later cleanup; callers must not modify it.
Call cute_tiled_free_external_tileset to free when done.

functions.name: cute_tiled_free_external_tileset
functions.description: Frees all dynamic memory associated with an external tileset previously returned by cute_tiled_load_external_tileset or cute_tiled_load_external_tileset_from_memory.
requirements: tileset must be a pointer returned by the corresponding load function.
Do not call more than once for the same tileset (no double-free).
Do not access tileset fields after freeing.

functions.name: cute_tiled_unset_flags
functions.description: Clears the Tiled flipping flag bits from a tile GID as stored in layer->data (CSV GIDs). Returns the raw tile ID with CUTE_TILED_FLIPPED_* bits masked out.
requirements: tile_data_gid is an integer GID possibly containing flip flags in the high bits.
Pure function with no side effects; safe for any int value.

functions.name: cute_tiled_get_flags
functions.signature: static CUTE_TILED_INLINE void cute_tiled_get_flags(int tile_data_gid, int* flip_horizontal, int* flip_vertical, int* flip_diagonal);
functions.description: Extracts the three Tiled flipping flags encoded in the high bits of a tile GID and writes them as 0/1 into the provided outputs.
requirements: flip_horizontal must be non-NULL.
flip_vertical must be non-NULL.
flip_diagonal must be non-NULL.
tile_data_gid should be the encoded GID value read from a layer’s data array.

functions.name: strpool_embedded_init
functions.signature: void strpool_embedded_init(strpool_embedded_t* pool, strpool_embedded_config_t const* config);
functions.description: Initializes a string pool with the provided configuration (or defaults if config is NULL). After initialization, the pool can inject strings and produce stable handles/cstrings.
requirements: pool must be non-NULL.
If config is not NULL, config->counter_bits + config->index_bits must be <= 64.
If config is NULL, strpool_embedded_default_config is used.
Must be called before any other strpool_embedded_* operation on the pool.

functions.name: strpool_embedded_term
functions.description: Tears down a previously initialized string pool and frees its internal allocations. After this, all handles/cstrings from the pool become invalid.
requirements: pool must be a pool previously initialized by strpool_embedded_init.
Do not use any handles or cstrings from this pool after termination.
Do not call twice on the same pool without re-initializing.

functions.name: strpool_embedded_inject
functions.signature: STRPOOL_EMBEDDED_U64 strpool_embedded_inject(strpool_embedded_t* pool, char const* string, int length);
functions.description: Interns a string into the pool and returns a 64-bit handle. If the string already exists (matching content and case-sensitivity mode), returns a handle to the existing entry. The pool stores the string and provides stable cstring pointers while alive.
requirements: pool must be initialized and non-NULL.
length must be >= 0.
If string is NULL or length < 0, the function returns handle 0 (invalid).
If the input pointer already points into the pool’s storage, it is recognized and its stored hash is reused.
The returned handle is only valid with the same pool and while the pool is alive.

functions.name: strpool_embedded_cstr
functions.signature: char const* strpool_embedded_cstr(strpool_embedded_t const* pool, STRPOOL_EMBEDDED_U64 handle);
functions.description: Resolves a previously returned handle to a NUL-terminated cstring stored in the pool. Returns NULL if the handle is invalid or not from this pool.
requirements: pool must be a valid, initialized pool pointer.
handle must be a valid handle previously returned by strpool_embedded_inject on the same pool.
Returned pointer is invalidated when strpool_embedded_term is called on the pool.

functions.name: cute_aseprite_load_from_file
functions.signature: ase_t* cute_aseprite_load_from_file(const char* path, void* mem_ctx);
functions.description: Loads and parses an .ase/.aseprite file from disk into an ase_t structure. Internally reads the file, then delegates to cute_aseprite_load_from_memory; frames are blended for convenience. Returns NULL if the file cannot be opened. On success, the returned ase_t owns allocated memory tied to mem_ctx and must be released with cute_aseprite_free. Warnings (e.g., unsupported blend modes) are emitted via CUTE_ASEPRITE_WARNING.
requirements: path must be a valid, readable filesystem path to a complete .ase/.aseprite file.
If custom allocators are used, CUTE_ASEPRITE_ALLOC/CUTE_ASEPRITE_FREE must be defined consistently and accept mem_ctx; mem_ctx is stored on the ase_t and used for all allocations/frees.
On non-NULL return, the caller must later call cute_aseprite_free(ase) exactly once to release all allocated resources.
To link the implementation, exactly one translation unit must define CUTE_ASEPRITE_IMPLEMENTATION before including this header.

functions.name: cute_aseprite_load_from_memory
functions.signature: ase_t* cute_aseprite_load_from_memory(const void* memory, int size, void* mem_ctx);
functions.description: Parses an .ase/.aseprite file already loaded in memory and constructs an ase_t with parsed content and pre-blended frame pixels. All memory for the resulting structure is allocated via CUTE_ASEPRITE_ALLOC using mem_ctx and recorded in ase->mem_ctx; free with cute_aseprite_free when done. Assertions enforce that the input buffer contains a valid, complete Aseprite file; warnings may be emitted for certain conditions (e.g., unsupported blend modes).
requirements: memory must point to the beginning of the complete .ase/.aseprite file data in memory; the buffer must contain the entire file.
size must be the exact byte length of the input buffer; insufficient size can trigger assertions or invalid reads.
The input data must be a valid Aseprite file (checks include magic 0xA5E0, proper chunk structure, etc.); otherwise assertions may fire.
If custom allocators are used, CUTE_ASEPRITE_ALLOC/CUTE_ASEPRITE_FREE must be defined consistently and accept mem_ctx; mem_ctx is stored on the ase_t and used for all allocations/frees.
The caller must call cute_aseprite_free on the returned pointer when finished to release resources.

functions.name: cute_aseprite_free
functions.description: Releases all memory owned by an ase_t previously returned by cute_aseprite_load_from_file or cute_aseprite_load_from_memory, including frames, cels, strings, palette names, and ICC profile data. Uses the mem_ctx stored in ase->mem_ctx and CUTE_ASEPRITE_FREE for deallocation.
requirements: ase must be a valid pointer previously returned by cute_aseprite_load_from_file or cute_aseprite_load_from_memory; it must not be NULL.
Must be called at most once per ase instance; using ase after this call is invalid.
The project must use the same allocator pair (CUTE_ASEPRITE_ALLOC/CUTE_ASEPRITE_FREE) and mem_ctx that were used to create the ase_t.

functions.name: cute_aseprite_warning
functions.signature: void cute_aseprite_warning(const char* warning, int line);
functions.description: Default warning handler used by this header when CUTE_ASEPRITE_WARNING is not user-defined. Prints a formatted warning to stdout including the header line number and the source of data (file path or MEMORY). Intended for internal use via the CUTE_ASEPRITE_WARNING(msg) macro; availability is conditional on not overriding the macro.
requirements: Only available if CUTE_ASEPRITE_WARNING is not predefined by the user; otherwise a user-provided macro handles warnings.
warning should be a non-NULL, NUL-terminated string.
line should be a non-negative integer, typically passed as __LINE__ by the macro.

functions.name: cs_error_as_string
functions.description: Returns a static C string describing a cs_error_t value. Useful for logging or debugging after an API call returns an error code.
requirements: error must be a valid cs_error_t enum value; unknown values return "UNKNOWN"

functions.name: cs_init
functions.signature: cs_error_t cs_init(void* os_handle, unsigned play_frequency_in_Hz, int buffered_samples, void* user_allocator_context /* = NULL */);
functions.description: Initializes the global cute_sound audio context and the selected backend (DirectSound on Windows, CoreAudio on Apple, SDL on others). Must be called before any other cute_sound API. Allocates internal buffers and starts/opens the device/driver as needed.
requirements: Must be called before any other cute_sound functions (except cs_error_as_string).
On Windows backend, os_handle must be a valid HWND; passing NULL returns CUTE_SOUND_ERROR_HWND_IS_NULL.
On Apple/SDL backends, pass NULL for os_handle.
play_frequency_in_Hz should match your audio data (e.g., 44100); used to configure the device.
buffered_samples is clamped to a minimum of 1024 internally.
user_allocator_context may be NULL; it is stored globally and passed to allocation macros.
Returns CUTE_SOUND_ERROR_NONE on success; otherwise one of the documented error codes.
On failure, no global context is available for use.

functions.name: cs_shutdown
functions.description: Shuts down the cute_sound system, stops/tears down the backend device, frees internal buffers, and releases all resources. Safe to call if not initialized; it returns immediately.
requirements: If a separate mixing thread was spawned, cs_shutdown waits for it to exit.
After cs_shutdown, the global context becomes NULL; no other cute_sound calls (besides another cs_init) should be made.
If there are playing sounds, they are cleaned up; any queued frees are processed.

functions.name: cs_update
functions.description: Per-tick update that advances music fades/switching/crossfades and, if no separate mixing thread is running, performs mixing on the calling thread.
requirements: cs_init must have succeeded before calling.
dt is a time delta in seconds; used for fade/crossfade timing.
If a separate mixing thread is spawned via cs_spawn_mix_thread, mixing occurs there; cs_update still advances music state.

functions.name: cs_set_global_volume
functions.description: Sets a global scalar applied to all audio (music and sounds). Values below 0 are clamped to 0. No upper clamp is applied beyond the global mix math.
requirements: cs_init must have succeeded before calling.
volume_0_to_1 is expected in [0,1]; values <0 are clamped to 0.

functions.name: cs_set_global_pan
functions.description: Sets a global pan applied to the mix (0 = full left, 1 = full right). Values are clamped to [0,1].
requirements: cs_init must have succeeded before calling.
pan_0_to_1 is clamped into [0,1].

functions.name: cs_set_global_pause
functions.description: Globally pauses or resumes mixing of all sounds and music when set. Paused sounds remain in the playing list but do not advance or mix.
requirements: cs_init must have succeeded before calling.

functions.name: cs_spawn_mix_thread
functions.description: Starts a background mixing thread so mixing no longer occurs inside cs_update. Subsequent calls are ignored if the thread is already running.
requirements: cs_init must have succeeded before calling.
Only call once per initialization; subsequent calls are no-ops.
On different backends it uses platform threading primitives; must not be called after cs_shutdown.

functions.name: cs_mix_thread_sleep_delay
functions.description: Sets an optional sleep/yield delay for the mixing loop to reduce CPU usage when idle. The delay is applied by the mixing thread on each loop iteration.
requirements: cs_init must have succeeded before calling.
milliseconds may be 0 (no sleep/yield); positive values increase sleep time.

functions.name: cs_get_context_ptr
functions.description: Returns the internal global context pointer (cs_context_t* as a void*). Useful for dynamic library usage or manual context management.
requirements: Must be called after cs_init or when a context has been set; may return NULL if not initialized.

functions.name: cs_set_context_ptr
functions.description: Overrides the global context pointer. Expert use only; primarily for dynamic library or custom context management scenarios.
requirements: ctx must be a valid cs_context_t* previously created/owned by cute_sound or the caller; invalid pointers will lead to undefined behavior.
Call only when you know what you are doing; function does not validate ctx.

functions.name: cs_load_wav
functions.signature: cs_audio_source_t* cs_load_wav(const char* path, cs_error_t* err /* = NULL */);
functions.description: Loads a PCM WAV file from disk into memory as a cs_audio_source_t suitable for playback. Supports mono or stereo, 16-bit PCM only.
requirements: cs_init is not strictly required to load, but freeing and playback rely on the global allocator/context.
path must refer to an existing RIFF WAVE file; otherwise returns NULL and sets *err.
Only PCM WAV, 1 or 2 channels, 16 bits per sample are supported; invalid formats set appropriate error codes.
On success, returns a heap-allocated cs_audio_source_t; must be freed with cs_free_audio_source when no longer used.

functions.name: cs_read_mem_wav
functions.signature: cs_audio_source_t* cs_read_mem_wav(const void* memory, size_t size, cs_error_t* err /* = NULL */);
functions.description: Parses a WAV file from a memory buffer and produces a cs_audio_source_t ready for playback. Supports PCM mono/stereo 16-bit samples.
requirements: memory must point to a valid RIFF WAVE blob of length size; returns NULL and sets *err if invalid.
Only PCM, 1 or 2 channels, 16 bits per sample are supported.
On success, caller must later free with cs_free_audio_source when no longer used.
If memory is NULL, sets *err = CUTE_SOUND_ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND and returns NULL.

functions.name: cs_free_audio_source
functions.description: Deallocates a cs_audio_source_t previously created by cs_load_wav/cs_read_mem_wav/cs_load_ogg/cs_read_mem_ogg. If the audio is still referenced by active plays, it is queued for deferred freeing until after playback finishes.
requirements: audio must be a pointer returned by the loader functions; double-freeing is undefined behavior.
If the global context exists and audio->playing_count > 0, the free is deferred; otherwise the audio is immediately freed.
Do not use the audio pointer after calling this function.

functions.name: cs_load_ogg
functions.signature: cs_audio_source_t* cs_load_ogg(const char* path, cs_error_t* err /* = NULL */);
functions.description: Loads an OGG/Vorbis file from disk using stb_vorbis into a cs_audio_source_t for playback. This API is available only if stb_vorbis was included before cute_sound.h (STB_VORBIS_INCLUDE_STB_VORBIS_H).
requirements: Requires STB_VORBIS_INCLUDE_STB_VORBIS_H to be defined before including cute_sound.h; otherwise this symbol is not declared/linked.
path must reference a valid OGG/Vorbis file; on decode failure, returns NULL and sets *err = CUTE_SOUND_ERROR_STB_VORBIS_DECODE_FAILED.
On success, the returned cs_audio_source_t must be freed with cs_free_audio_source.

functions.name: cs_read_mem_ogg
functions.signature: cs_audio_source_t* cs_read_mem_ogg(const void* memory, size_t length, cs_error_t* err /* = NULL */);
functions.description: Decodes OGG/Vorbis audio from a memory buffer using stb_vorbis, producing a cs_audio_source_t for playback. Available only when stb_vorbis was included before cute_sound.h.
requirements: Requires STB_VORBIS_INCLUDE_STB_VORBIS_H to be defined before including cute_sound.h; otherwise this symbol is unavailable.
memory must point to an OGG/Vorbis byte stream of given length; on failure returns NULL and sets *err = CUTE_SOUND_ERROR_STB_VORBIS_DECODE_FAILED.
Only mono or stereo files are supported; other channel counts set *err = CUTE_SOUND_ERROR_OGG_UNSUPPORTED_CHANNEL_COUNT.
On success, free the result via cs_free_audio_source.

functions.name: cs_load_wav_rw
functions.signature: cs_audio_source_t* cs_load_wav_rw(SDL_RWops* context, cs_error_t* err /* = NULL */);
functions.description: Loads WAV data from an SDL_RWops stream into a cs_audio_source_t. Intended for use with SDL backends when CUTE_SOUND_SDL_RWOPS is enabled.

functions.name: cp_inflate

functions.description: Decompresses a raw DEFLATE bitstream (RFC 1951, without zlib header) from the input buffer into the output buffer. Intended for cases where the uncompressed size is already known. Performs strict bounds checks and sets cp_error_reason on failure. Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: in must point to a raw DEFLATE stream (no zlib header/footer).

out must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the entire uncompressed output.
out_bytes must equal the intended uncompressed size; the function will fail if it would write past out or before out.
Buffers must not overlap in a way that violates standard memcopy semantics (function assumes separate in/out).
On error, cp_error_reason may contain a human-readable message.
