functions.description: Encodes an RGBA image (8-bit/channel) and writes it as a PNG file to disk using fixed-Huffman DEFLATE and standard PNG chunks (IHDR/IDAT/IEND). Returns 1 for success and 0 for failure per API docs. Note: the current implementation returns 1 if fopen fails and !ferror(fp) otherwise, which may not match the documented convention; treat non-zero as “no write error detected,” but be aware of this inconsistency.
requirements: file_name must be a valid writable path; the directory must exist.
img must be non-NULL and point to a valid cp_image_t with img->w >= 0, img->h >= 0, and img->pix != NULL pointing to img->w * img->h pixels of cp_pixel_t in RGBA order.
Caller should check the return value; non-zero indicates success by intended API design (but see note about implementation inconsistency).
On success/failure writing to disk depends on the underlying C I/O; no exceptions are thrown.
This function does not free or modify the input image.

functions.name: cp_save_png_to_memory
functions.description: Encodes an RGBA image (8-bit/channel) to a PNG and returns the result in an allocated memory buffer. Use CUTE_PNG_FREE on the returned .data when done. On error, returns { size=0, data=NULL }. No exceptions are thrown.
requirements: img must be non-NULL and reference a valid cp_image_t with img->pix != NULL and dimensions set.
Caller must free the returned .data using CUTE_PNG_FREE when done (if data is non-NULL).
Returned buffer is exactly .size bytes; it contains a complete PNG file (signature + chunks).

functions.name: cp_make_atlas
functions.signature: cp_image_t cp_make_atlas(int atlasWidth, int atlasHeight, const cp_image_t* pngs, int png_count, cp_atlas_image_t* imgs_out);
functions.description: Packs multiple RGBA images into a single atlas of size atlasWidth x atlasHeight. Returns the atlas image; atlas_image.pix is NULL on failure. Fills imgs_out with placement info (u/v bounds, dimensions, fit flag, and original index). If CUTE_PNG_ATLAS_MUST_FIT is 1, the function fails if any image cannot fit; otherwise, images that do not fit are marked fit=0 and skipped.
requirements: pngs must be non-NULL and point to an array of png_count cp_image_t, each with valid w, h, and pix.
imgs_out must be non-NULL and point to an array of png_count cp_atlas_image_t for output metadata.
atlasWidth and atlasHeight should be positive; the atlas is created exactly with those dimensions.
Caller must free the returned cp_image_t.pix using CUTE_PNG_FREE/free when done (if not NULL).
If CUTE_PNG_ATLAS_MUST_FIT == 1 and not all images fit, the function returns an image with pix == NULL and sets cp_error_reason.
UVs are optionally Y-flipped if CUTE_PNG_ATLAS_FLIP_Y_AXIS_FOR_UV is defined (default 1).
Empty regions are filled with CUTE_PNG_ATLAS_EMPTY_COLOR (RGBA).

functions.name: cp_default_save_atlas
functions.signature: int cp_default_save_atlas(const char* out_path_image, const char* out_path_atlas_txt, const cp_image_t* atlas, const cp_atlas_image_t* imgs, int img_count, const char** names);
functions.description: Writes atlas metadata to a simple text file and saves the atlas image PNG to disk. The text lists, for each placed image, its size and u/v coordinates; names can be NULL or an array indexed by original image index. Intended to return non-zero on error by example usage; however, the current implementation returns 0 unconditionally, which makes error signaling unreliable.
requirements: out_path_atlas_txt must be a writable path; the directory must exist.
out_path_image must be a writable path for the atlas image; used by cp_save_png.
atlas must point to a valid cp_image_t with pix set to the atlas pixels.
imgs must be a valid array of img_count cp_atlas_image_t previously produced by cp_make_atlas.
names can be NULL; if non-NULL, it must be indexable by imgs[i].img_index.
Callers should not rely on the return value to detect errors due to the implementation returning 0 always; external verification (e.g., file existence) may be necessary.

functions.name: cp_load_png
functions.description: Loads a PNG file from disk into an RGBA cp_image_t. Supports 8-bit depth, standard DEFLATE compression, standard PNG adaptive filtering, and no interlacing. Returns img with pix == NULL on failure. Sets cp_error_reason on parse/validation errors.
requirements: file_name must be a readable path to a PNG file.
Only 8-bit PNGs are supported; interlaced PNGs are not supported; only standard DEFLATE compression and filtering are supported.
Caller must free img.pix with CUTE_PNG_FREE/free or call cp_free_png when done.
On failure, returns {w=0,h=0,pix=NULL} and may set cp_error_reason with a diagnostic.

functions.name: cp_load_png_mem
functions.description: Parses and decodes a PNG from memory into an RGBA cp_image_t. Supports 8-bit depth, color types 0 (gray), 2 (RGB), 3 (indexed), 4 (gray+alpha), 6 (RGBA), standard DEFLATE compression, standard filtering, and no interlacing. For indexed images, applies PLTE and optional tRNS to produce RGBA. Returns img with pix == NULL on failure and sets cp_error_reason.
requirements: png_data must point to the complete PNG file bytes and png_length must be the exact size.
PNG signature must be present; IHDR must be valid with bit depth 8 and supported color type.
Only standard DEFLATE compression (zlib method 8), no preset dictionary, appropriate window size, standard filtering, and no interlace are supported; otherwise the function fails.
Image size must not overflow internal limits; extremely large images are rejected.
Caller must free img.pix with CUTE_PNG_FREE/free or call cp_free_png when done.
On failure, returns {w=?,h=?,pix=NULL} (w/h may be 0) and cp_error_reason may describe the error.

functions.name: cp_load_blank
functions.description: Allocates a cp_image_t of size w x h with an uninitialized pixel buffer. Intended for callers that will fill pixel data manually.
requirements: w and h should be non-negative; behavior is undefined for negative sizes.
The returned img.pix must be freed with CUTE_PNG_FREE/free or via cp_free_png.
Pixels are uninitialized; caller must set them before use.

functions.name: cp_free_png
functions.description: Frees the pixel buffer of a cp_image_t and resets w and h to 0. Safe to call on imgs with pix == NULL.
requirements: img must be non-NULL and point to a cp_image_t.
img->pix must have been allocated with CUTE_PNG_ALLOC/malloc-compatible allocator; this function uses CUTE_PNG_FREE to release it.
After the call, img->pix is set to NULL and dimensions are zeroed.

functions.name: cp_flip_image_horizontal
functions.description: Flips the image in-place across the horizontal axis (top and bottom rows swapped). Despite the name, the implementation performs a vertical flip (Y-axis inversion).
requirements: img must be non-NULL and point to a valid cp_image_t with pix != NULL.
img->pix must be writable; operation is in-place.
Function assumes tightly packed rows of width img->w and type cp_pixel_t.

functions.name: cp_load_png_wh
functions.signature: void cp_load_png_wh(const void* png_data, int png_length, int* w, int* h);
functions.description: Reads only the width and height from a PNG in memory without full decoding. On failure, outputs 0 for provided outputs. Does minimal validation (signature and IHDR).
requirements: png_data must point to the complete PNG file bytes and png_length must be their size.
w and/or h may be NULL; non-NULL outputs are set to 0 on failure and to the image dimensions on success.
Only the PNG header (IHDR) is inspected; no image decoding is performed.
Dimensions reported are the IHDR width and height.

functions.name: cp_load_indexed_png
functions.description: Loads a paletted (indexed, color type 3) PNG from disk without depalettizing. Returns pixel indices and expands the palette (PLTE and optional tRNS) into cp_indexed_image_t.palette. Returns img with pix == NULL on failure and sets cp_error_reason.
requirements: file_name must be a readable path to a PNG file.
Only 8-bit indexed PNGs (color type 3, bit depth 8) are supported; standard DEFLATE compression, standard filtering, and no interlacing are required.
Caller must free img.pix with CUTE_PNG_FREE/free or call cp_free_indexed_png when done.
On failure, returns {w=0,h=0,pix=NULL} (palette may be undefined) and cp_error_reason may describe the error.

functions.name: cp_load_indexed_png_mem
functions.description: Parses and decodes an indexed (paletted) PNG from memory into cp_indexed_image_t. Produces the index buffer and fills the palette from PLTE and optional tRNS. Returns img with pix == NULL on failure and sets cp_error_reason.
requirements: png_data must point to the complete PNG file bytes and png_length must be the exact size.
Only 8-bit indexed PNGs (color type 3) are accepted; PLTE must be present.
Requires standard DEFLATE compression (zlib method 8), no preset dictionary, appropriate window size, standard filtering, and no interlacing.
Caller must free img.pix with CUTE_PNG_FREE/free or call cp_free_indexed_png when done.
On failure, returns {w=?,h=?,pix=NULL} and cp_error_reason may describe the error.

functions.name: cp_free_indexed_png
functions.description: Frees the pixel index buffer of a cp_indexed_image_t and resets w and h to 0. Palette fields are left as-is.
requirements: img must be non-NULL and point to a cp_indexed_image_t.
img->pix must have been allocated with CUTE_PNG_ALLOC/malloc-compatible allocator; this function uses CUTE_PNG_FREE to release it.
After the call, img->pix is set to NULL and dimensions are zeroed.

functions.name: cp_depallete_indexed_image
functions.description: Converts an indexed image to a standard RGBA cp_image_t using the image’s palette (with alpha possibly from tRNS). Allocates a new cp_image_t and copies pixels. The returned image must be freed by the caller.
requirements: img must be non-NULL and contain valid dimensions and a non-NULL index buffer (img->pix).
img->palette_len and palette contents should correctly represent the PLTE/tRNS data for accurate conversion.
Caller must free the returned cp_image_t.pix with CUTE_PNG_FREE/free or via cp_free_png.

functions.name: cp_premultiply
functions.description: Pre-multiplies RGB channels by alpha in-place for an RGBA image. Useful for rendering pipelines expecting premultiplied alpha. Operates on 8-bit channels, writing back to the same buffer.
requirements: img must be non-NULL and point to a valid cp_image_t with pix != NULL and dimensions set.
Pixels must be in RGBA 8-bit format laid out as cp_pixel_t.
Operation is destructive; do not call if you need unmodified colors.

functions.name: spritebatch_push
functions.description: Pushes a sprite into the spritebatch input buffer; no sorting or rendering occurs here. The sprite’s UVs and texture_id may be overwritten later during processing. Returns 1 on success.
requirements: sb must be a valid, initialized spritebatch_t (spritebatch_init previously succeeded).
sprite.image_id must be set to a unique identifier for the image.
sprite.w and sprite.h must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to sb->atlas_width_in_pixels and sb->atlas_height_in_pixels respectively (asserted in spritebatch_internal_fill_internal_sprite).
sprite.texture_id and sprite.sort_bits can be 0; UVs (minx/miny/maxx/maxy) will be assigned later.
If SPRITEBATCH_SPRITE_GEOMETRY_DEFAULT is used and atlas border pixels are enabled, internal code adjusts sx/sy automatically.

functions.name: spritebatch_prefetch
functions.signature: void spritebatch_prefetch(spritebatch_t* sb, SPRITEBATCH_U64 image_id, int w, int h);
functions.description: Hints/ensures that the texture needed for image_id is prepared by the batcher without actually drawing a sprite. Useful to pre-load imminent images (e.g., upcoming animation frames).
requirements: sb must be a valid, initialized spritebatch_t.
image_id identifies the image to prefetch.
w and h are the image’s pixel dimensions and must be correct for the image. If a new lonely texture record is created internally, these dimensions are used for allocation/handle generation later.
May trigger creating an entry in the lonely-texture cache (possibly without GPU handle until needed).

functions.name: spritebatch_invalidate
functions.description: Invalidates internal cache entries for a given image_id. If the image was in an atlas, the entire atlas is flushed; if it was a lonely texture, that texture entry is removed so pixels can be reuploaded on next use.
requirements: sb must be valid and initialized.
image_id must reference a previously known image (if not found, the function simply does nothing).
Call when underlying image pixels change and must be reflected immediately.

functions.name: spritebatch_fetch
functions.signature: spritebatch_sprite_t spritebatch_fetch(spritebatch_t* sb, SPRITEBATCH_U64 image_id, int w, int h);
functions.description: Returns a spritebatch_sprite_t populated with texture_id and UVs for the specified image_id so the caller can render it via an external renderer (e.g., Dear ImGui). The result is valid until the next call to spritebatch_defrag.
requirements: sb must be initialized.
If image_id is not in a premade atlas or internal atlas, w and h must be correct for the image to generate or look up a lonely texture.
Returned sprite’s UVs/texture_id may change after spritebatch_defrag; do not cache beyond that point.

functions.name: spritebatch_tick
functions.description: Advances internal timestamps for textures in atlases and lonely textures by one tick. Used by defragmentation/decay logic.
requirements: sb must be initialized.
Typically called once per frame/tick to support decay policies referenced by spritebatch_defrag.

functions.name: spritebatch_flush
functions.description: Sorts pushed sprites and submits them in batches that share texture_id via the user-provided submit callback. Ensures any missing lonely texture GPU handles are created. Returns the number of submitted batches.
requirements: sb must be initialized and have valid callbacks set (batch_callback, get_pixels_callback, generate_texture_callback, delete_texture_callback; sorter optional).
Call after pushing sprites via spritebatch_push. This may call get_pixels_fn and generate_texture_handle_fn if required.
Return value is the count of submit_batch_fn calls performed.
After flush, sb->sprite_count is reset to 0.

functions.name: spritebatch_defrag
functions.description: Performs internal atlas management: decays/removes old atlases, merges small atlases, moves recently used images into new atlases from the lonely buffer, and may free decayed lonely textures. Can be called periodically (e.g., every N ticks). Returns 1.
requirements: sb must be initialized.
Relies on sb config parameters (ticks_to_decay_texture, ratio_to_decay_atlas, ratio_to_merge_atlases, lonely_buffer_count_till_flush/decay).
May call delete_texture_callback for textures being freed; caller’s callback must tolerate being called from this function.
May rebuild atlases which changes UVs and texture_id mappings for images.

functions.name: spritebatch_init
functions.signature: int spritebatch_init(spritebatch_t* sb, spritebatch_config_t* config, void* udata);
functions.description: Initializes the spritebatch context with the provided configuration and user data pointer. Allocates internal buffers and validates configuration. Returns 0 on success, 1 on failure.
requirements: sb and config must be non-null (function returns 1 if null).
config->atlas_width_in_pixels and atlas_height_in_pixels must be >= 1.
config->ticks_to_decay_texture must be >= 1.
config->ratio_to_decay_atlas must be in [0, 1].
config->ratio_to_merge_atlases must be in [0, 0.5].
config callbacks must be non-null: batch_callback, get_pixels_callback, generate_texture_callback, delete_texture_callback. sprites_sorter_callback is optional.
On success, sb holds allocations that must later be released by spritebatch_term.
udata is stored and later passed to callbacks.

functions.name: spritebatch_term
functions.description: Tears down the spritebatch context: frees internal buffers, hashtables, and atlas structures, and zeroes the sb struct. Intended to be paired with spritebatch_init.
requirements: sb must have been initialized by spritebatch_init; passing an uninitialized or partially-initialized sb may lead to invalid frees.
After return, sb is zeroed and must be re-initialized before reuse.

functions.name: spritebatch_register_premade_atlas
functions.signature: void spritebatch_register_premade_atlas(spritebatch_t* sb, SPRITEBATCH_U64 texture_id, int w, int h, int sprite_count, spritebatch_premade_sprite_t* sprites);
functions.description: Registers a prebuilt atlas (texture_id with atlas dimensions w/h) and an array of sprites mapping image_id to UVs in that atlas. Subsequent pushes/fetches for those image_ids will use this premade atlas.
requirements: sb must be initialized.
sprites must point to an array of sprite_count entries; each entry’s image_id must be unique across the batcher and refer to that premade atlas.
w and h are the atlas texture dimensions in pixels; must match the provided texture’s size.
texture_id must be a valid texture handle recognizable by the caller’s renderer.

functions.name: spritebatch_reset_function_ptrs
functions.signature: void spritebatch_reset_function_ptrs(spritebatch_t* sb, submit_batch_fn* batch_callback, get_pixels_fn* get_pixels_callback, generate_texture_handle_fn* generate_texture_handle_callback, destroy_texture_handle_fn* delete_texture_callback, sprites_sorter_fn* sprites_sorter_callback);
functions.description: Resets all function pointers used by the batcher (submit, get-pixels, generate/destroy texture handle, and optional sorter). Useful after DLL reloads or when swapping backends.
requirements: sb must be initialized.
batch_callback, get_pixels_callback, generate_texture_handle_callback, and delete_texture_callback should be non-null for subsequent operations; sprites_sorter_callback is optional.
After changing callbacks, ensure the new implementations are compatible with any previously created texture handles.

functions.name: spritebatch_set_default_config
functions.description: Fills a spritebatch_config_t with sensible defaults (e.g., RGBA8 stride, 2048x2048 atlas, decay/merge ratios). Does not set the required callbacks; caller must set them before spritebatch_init.
requirements: config must be non-null and writable.
After calling, set at least batch_callback, get_pixels_callback, generate_texture_callback, and delete_texture_callback before initialization.

functions.name: hashtable_init
functions.signature: void hashtable_init(hashtable_t* table, int item_size, int initial_capacity, void* memctx);
functions.description: Initializes a cache-efficient open-addressed hash table for fixed-size items keyed by 64-bit keys. Allocates internal storage using memctx.
requirements: table must be non-null and writable.
item_size must be > 0 (used for allocations and copies).
initial_capacity can be any integer; internally clamped to a power-of-two minimum.
memctx is an allocator context pointer passed through to HASHTABLE_MALLOC/FREE macros (may be null depending on allocator).
Table must later be freed with hashtable_term.

functions.name: hashtable_term
functions.description: Releases memory owned by a previously initialized hashtable_t. Does not free items beyond table-owned contiguous storage.
requirements: table must have been initialized by hashtable_init.
Do not use the table after termination unless reinitialized.

functions.name: hashtable_insert
functions.signature: void* hashtable_insert(hashtable_t* table, HASHTABLE_U64 key, void const* item);
functions.description: Inserts a new key-item pair and returns a writable pointer to the stored item slot. The item data is copied by value into the table’s storage. Keys must be unique.
requirements: table must be initialized.
key must not already exist in the table (enforced by assertion).
item must point to at least item_size bytes to copy from.
May reallocate internal storage; returned pointer may be invalidated by subsequent rehashing/expansion operations.

functions.name: hashtable_remove
functions.description: Removes an existing key from the table, compacting internal arrays as needed.
requirements: table must be initialized.
key must exist in the table (enforced by assertion).
Any previously cached item pointers may be invalidated after removal.

functions.name: hashtable_clear
functions.description: Clears all items from the table without freeing capacity, resetting slot metadata.
requirements: table must be initialized.
All previously obtained item pointers become invalid after this call.

functions.name: hashtable_find
functions.signature: void* hashtable_find(hashtable_t const* table, HASHTABLE_U64 key);
functions.description: Finds and returns a pointer to the stored item for the given key, or NULL if not present. Pointer is to internal contiguous storage.
requirements: table must be initialized.
Returned pointer is invalidated by any operation that changes the table’s storage (insert, remove, clear, term, or rehash).

functions.name: hashtable_count
functions.description: Returns the number of items currently stored in the table.
requirements: table must be initialized.

functions.name: hashtable_items
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the contiguous array of stored items (count = hashtable_count(table)). Items are in an internal order that can change as the table mutates.
requirements: table must be initialized.
Returned pointer is invalidated by any mutating operation on the table (insert, remove, clear, term, or rehash).
Interpretation of the data requires the caller to know item_size used at init.

functions.name: hashtable_keys
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the contiguous array of keys parallel to hashtable_items’ item storage.
requirements: table must be initialized.
Returned pointer is invalidated by any mutating operation on the table (insert, remove, clear, term, or rehash).
Array length equals hashtable_count(table).

functions.name: hashtable_swap
functions.signature: void hashtable_swap(hashtable_t* table, int index_a, int index_b);
functions.description: Swaps items and their keys at the specified indices within the internal contiguous arrays, updating slot backreferences. No-op if either index is out of range.
requirements: table must be initialized.
index_a and index_b must be in [0, hashtable_count(table)) to have an effect.
Any previously cached item pointers remain valid as the swap happens in-place, but item order changes.

functions.name: cute_mutex_create
functions.description: Creates and returns a new, unlocked mutex object. The mutex is a small value type (union) that can be stored on the stack or embedded in other structs. Intended for protecting shared data across threads.
requirements: No arguments required.
Use the returned mutex only after initialization via this function.
Destroy with cute_mutex_destroy when no longer needed.
Do not copy the mutex after use has begun; treat it as non-copyable once shared across threads.

functions.name: cute_lock
functions.description: Locks the given mutex, blocking the calling thread until the lock is acquired. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise (per documented contract).
requirements: mutex must be a valid pointer to a mutex created by cute_mutex_create.
The same thread must eventually call cute_unlock on the same mutex to release it.
Do not pass NULL.
Undefined behavior if the mutex has been destroyed or not initialized.

functions.name: cute_unlock
functions.description: Unlocks the given mutex. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise (per documented contract).
requirements: mutex must be a valid pointer previously locked by the calling thread.
Do not pass NULL.
Undefined behavior if the mutex was not owned by the calling thread or has been destroyed.

functions.name: cute_trylock
functions.description: Attempts to acquire the mutex without blocking. Returns 1 if the lock was acquired, 0 otherwise.
requirements: mutex must be a valid pointer to a mutex created by cute_mutex_create.
Do not pass NULL.
If 1 is returned, the caller must later call cute_unlock on the mutex.
May fail spuriously if already locked by another thread.

functions.name: cute_mutex_destroy
functions.description: Destroys the given mutex and releases any associated OS resources.
requirements: mutex must be a valid pointer to a mutex created by cute_mutex_create.
The mutex must not be in use by any thread when destroyed (must not be locked).
Do not pass NULL.
After destruction, the mutex must not be used again.

functions.name: cute_cv_create
functions.description: Creates and returns a condition variable used to block and wake threads in coordination with a mutex.
requirements: No arguments required.
Use with a mutex created by cute_mutex_create.
Destroy with cute_cv_destroy when no longer needed.

functions.name: cute_cv_wake_all
functions.description: Signals all threads waiting on the condition variable to wake. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: cv must be a valid pointer to a condition variable created by cute_cv_create.
Do not pass NULL.
Typically called while holding the associated mutex (standard condition variable practice).
Undefined behavior if cv has been destroyed or not initialized.

functions.name: cute_cv_wake_one
functions.description: Signals a single thread waiting on the condition variable to wake. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: cv must be a valid pointer to a condition variable created by cute_cv_create.
Do not pass NULL.
Typically called while holding the associated mutex.
Undefined behavior if cv has been destroyed or not initialized.

functions.name: cute_cv_wait
functions.description: Atomically releases the provided mutex and blocks the calling thread on the condition variable. Upon wakeup, re-acquires the mutex before returning. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: cv must be a valid pointer created by cute_cv_create.
mutex must be a valid pointer to a mutex created by cute_mutex_create, associated with this wait.
The calling thread must hold the mutex before calling cute_cv_wait.
Do not pass NULL for either parameter.
Undefined behavior if cv/mutex are destroyed while waiting.

functions.name: cute_cv_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a condition variable and releases associated resources.
requirements: cv must be a valid pointer created by cute_cv_create.
No threads should be waiting on the condition variable at the time of destruction.
Do not pass NULL.
After destruction, cv must not be used again.

functions.name: cute_semaphore_create
functions.description: Creates a semaphore with the given initial count. On some platforms, failure results in an internal NULL handle. Note: Although an earlier comment says “Returns NULL on failure”, this function returns a value type; check internal handle for failure if accessible.
requirements: initial_count should be >= 0 (typical semaphore requirement; sem_init takes unsigned).
On failure, the internal field may be NULL; callers that can see cute_semaphore_t should check semaphore.id != NULL before use.
Destroy with cute_semaphore_destroy when done.

functions.name: cute_semaphore_post
functions.description: Atomically increments the semaphore and wakes one waiting thread. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: semaphore must be a valid pointer to a semaphore created by cute_semaphore_create.
Do not pass NULL.
Undefined behavior if semaphore has been destroyed.

functions.name: cute_semaphore_try
functions.description: Non-blocking attempt to decrement the semaphore if its count is positive. Returns 1 on success (acquired), 0 otherwise.
requirements: semaphore must be a valid pointer created by cute_semaphore_create.
Do not pass NULL.

functions.name: cute_semaphore_wait
functions.description: Blocks the calling thread until the semaphore count is positive, then decrements it atomically. Returns 1 on success, 0 otherwise.
requirements: semaphore must be a valid pointer created by cute_semaphore_create.
Do not pass NULL.
May block indefinitely if not posted elsewhere.

functions.name: cute_semaphore_value
functions.description: Returns the current value of the semaphore’s count (best-effort according to the platform implementation).
requirements: semaphore must be a valid pointer created by cute_semaphore_create.
Do not pass NULL.
Value may be transient in concurrent contexts.

functions.name: cute_semaphore_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a semaphore and frees any associated resources.
requirements: semaphore must be a valid pointer created by cute_semaphore_create.
Ensure no threads are waiting on the semaphore during destruction.
Do not pass NULL.
After destruction, semaphore must not be used again.

functions.name: cute_thread_create
functions.signature: cute_thread_t* cute_thread_create(cute_thread_fn func, const char* name, void* udata)
functions.description: Creates a new thread that begins execution at func(udata). name is optional and may be used by some platforms for thread naming. Returns an opaque thread handle pointer, or possibly NULL on failure (platform-dependent).
requirements: func must be a valid function pointer of type int (*)(void*).
name may be NULL.
udata may be NULL.
Caller must later call cute_thread_wait to join the thread, or cute_thread_detach if it will not be joined.
Do not reuse the returned handle after detaching or after wait closes it (platform dependent).

functions.name: cute_thread_detach
functions.description: Detaches a thread, indicating it will not be joined. This is an optimization for long-lived or fire-and-forget threads.
requirements: thread must be a valid handle returned by cute_thread_create.
It is invalid to call cute_thread_wait on a detached thread.
Do not call cute_thread_detach more than once on the same thread.
After detaching, the handle must not be used with cute_thread_wait.

functions.name: cute_thread_get_id
functions.description: Returns the OS thread ID for the given thread handle.
requirements: thread must be a valid handle returned by cute_thread_create.
Do not pass NULL.
Behavior is undefined if called on a detached and already-terminated thread on platforms where the handle was closed by detach.

functions.name: cute_thread_id
functions.description: Returns the current thread’s OS thread ID.
requirements: No arguments required.

functions.name: cute_thread_wait
functions.description: Blocks until the thread exits (or returns immediately if it already exited), then returns the thread’s return code when available. On detached threads, calling this is invalid. Return value may be implementation-dependent on some platforms.
requirements: thread must be a valid handle returned by cute_thread_create.

functions.name: tls_connect
functions.signature: TLS_Connection tls_connect(const char* hostname, int port);
functions.description: Creates and initializes a new TLS 1.2 client connection context for the specified hostname and TCP port. It initiates a non-blocking TCP connect and sets up the TLS handshake state; callers should then poll tls_process until the state transitions to TLS_STATE_CONNECTED or an error. On success, returns a nonzero TLS_Connection handle that must later be closed with tls_disconnect; on failure returns a zero-initialized handle.
requirements: hostname must be a valid, null-terminated host name or address string accepted by getaddrinfo.
port should be a valid TCP port in the range 1..65535; 0 or negative values are invalid.
The returned TLS_Connection must be eventually released with tls_disconnect to avoid leaks.
After calling tls_connect, the caller should repeatedly call tls_process to drive the TCP connect and TLS handshake before attempting tls_send/tls_read.
The connection handle is only valid if nonzero (id != 0).

functions.name: tls_disconnect
functions.description: Closes the TLS session and underlying TCP socket and frees all resources associated with the given TLS_Connection. Sends a TLS close-notify when applicable and drains/frees any queued receive buffers.
requirements: connection must be a handle previously returned by tls_connect and not already disconnected.
Do not use the connection for tls_process, tls_read, or tls_send after calling tls_disconnect.
Call exactly once per successful tls_connect to release resources (no double-free).

functions.name: tls_process
functions.description: Advances the connection state machine. While pending, it progresses the non-blocking TCP connect and performs the TLS handshake. Once connected, it services I/O by receiving from the socket, decrypting, and queueing application data for tls_read. Returns the current TLS_State (negative on errors).
requirements: connection must be a valid handle from tls_connect and not yet disconnected.
Call in a loop after tls_connect until it returns TLS_STATE_CONNECTED or a negative error state.
Continue calling periodically after connected to pull incoming data and feed the internal packet queue.
If it returns TLS_STATE_PACKET_QUEUE_FILLED, the caller should drain data via tls_read before further processing.
Do not expect tls_process to block; it is designed for polling.

functions.name: tls_state_string
functions.description: Returns a string constant describing the given TLS_State value, or NULL if the state is not recognized. Useful for logging or error reporting.
requirements: state should be a TLS_State enumeration value returned by tls_process or otherwise defined in the TLS_State enum.
Caller must not modify or free the returned string pointer.

functions.name: tls_read
functions.signature: int tls_read(TLS_Connection connection, void* data, int size);
functions.description: Copies up to size bytes of received application data into the caller’s buffer from the internal packet queue. Returns the number of bytes copied on success, 0 if no data is currently available (or after disconnect when the queue has been drained), and -1 if the connection is in an error state.
requirements: connection must be valid and not in an error state; if ctx state < 0 the function returns -1.
data must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
size must be non-negative.
Call after tls_process has been run to populate the internal receive queue; repeated calls may be needed to consume all data.

If tls_process previously returned TLS_STATE_DISCONNECTED_BUT_PACKETS_STILL_REMAIN, continue calling tls_read until it returns 0, at which point the internal state transitions to TLS_STATE_DISCONNECTED.

functions.name: tls_send
functions.signature: int tls_send(TLS_Connection connection, const void* data, int size);
functions.description: Encrypts and sends size bytes from data over the active TLS connection. Returns 0 on success and -1 on error. On Windows and s2n backends it may internally loop until all data is written (non-blocking-friendly); on Apple it dispatches an async send and reports errors by transitioning the connection state.
requirements: connection must be in a positive (nonzero) state; calling when state <= 0 fails. Intended for use after tls_process reports TLS_STATE_CONNECTED.
data must point to at least size bytes of readable memory.
size must be non-negative; sending 0 bytes is a no-op that succeeds.
Caller should handle a return value of -1 as a send failure and treat the connection state as potentially transitioned to an error.
Do not call after tls_disconnect.

data_types.description: An arbitrary NUL-terminated UTF-8/ASCII string used as a generic message or label. No specific format or encoding constraints beyond being a typical C-style string; may be empty or contain any bytes except embedded NUL for most APIs expecting a C string.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
import string

# Target data type: text string (C-style NUL-terminated), used via FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
# Fuzzer stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain a std::string whose c_str() is
# passed to cn_error_failure. We want interesting, but valid, C strings.
# The harness will likely copy our bytes directly as the fuzzable blob that
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumes. Typical fuzzers map the provided bytes to produce
# one or more strings; here we provide a single NUL-terminated payload, and
# optionally multiple concatenated NUL-terminated strings to exercise empty,
# long, unicode-ish, and edge-case contents in one buffer.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "

# Some interesting substrings that resemble common messages and edge cases.
INTERESTING_STRINGS = [
    "",  # empty string
    " ",
    "error",
    "warning",
    "info",
    "ok",
    "SUCCESS",
    "FAILURE",
    "null",
    "NULL",
    "(null)",
    "none",
    "\n",        # newline only
    "\r\n",     # CRLF
    "\t",       # tab
    "%s %d %p", # printf-like
    "%%s %%d %%p",
    "errno=0",
    "errno=22",
    "127.0.0.1:5000",
    "[::1]:5000",
    "C:\\path\\to\\file.txt",
    "/tmp/test.sock",
    "🧪 fuzz test",  # UTF-8
    "∅",
    "こんにちは",
    "Привет",
    "mañana",
    "naïve",
    "über",
    "very-long-message-",
]

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_utf8_chunk(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII with some multi-byte code points.
    out = []
    while len(''.join(out).encode('utf-8')) < n:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.7:
            out.append(rng.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE))
        else:
            # pick from a few ranges
            cp_choices = [
                rng.randrange(0x00A1, 0x017F),   # Latin-1 Supplement + Latin Extended-A
                rng.randrange(0x0400, 0x04FF),   # Cyrillic
                rng.randrange(0x0370, 0x03FF),   # Greek
                rng.randrange(0x3040, 0x30FF),   # Hiragana/Katakana
                rng.randrange(0x1F300, 0x1F64F), # Misc symbols/emojis
            ]
            ch = chr(rng.choice(cp_choices))
            out.append(ch)
    s = ''.join(out)
    # Trim to target byte size
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    return b[:n].decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')

def _make_variants(rng: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    variants: list[bytes] = []

    # 1) Empty string
    variants.append(b"\x00")

    # 2) Short ASCII tokens
    tokens = [rng.choice(INTERESTING_STRINGS) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5))]
    s2 = ' '.join(tokens)
    variants.append(s2.encode('utf-8', 'ignore') + b"\x00")

    # 3) Random ASCII length 1..64
    n3 = rng.randint(1, 64)
    s3 = _rand_ascii(rng, n3)
    variants.append(s3.encode('ascii') + b"\x00")

    # 4) Random UTF-8 chunk length ~32..128 bytes
    n4 = rng.randint(32, 128)
    s4 = _rand_utf8_chunk(rng, n4)
    variants.append(s4.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # 5) Long line with newlines and special chars
    parts = [
        rng.choice(["ERROR:", "WARN:", "INFO:", "DEBUG:"]),
        _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(10, 40)),
        "|file=", rng.choice(["main.cpp", "net.c", "tls.c", "server.cc"]),
        ":", str(rng.randint(1, 5000)),
        "\n",
        _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(5, 20)),
    ]
    s5 = ''.join(parts)
    variants.append(s5.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # 6) Format-string like, with percent and braces
    fmt = rng.choice([
        "{level}:{code}:{msg}",
        "%LEVEL%:%CODE%:%MSG%",
        "%s:%d:%p",
        "[%s] (%d) -> %p",
    ])
    variants.append(fmt.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # 7) Repeated pattern to reach a larger size but within limits
    base = rng.choice(["ABCD", "0123", "==", "--", "::"]) * rng.randint(8, 64)
    variants.append(base.encode('ascii') + b"\x00")

    # 8) Unicode-heavy string
    u = rng.choice(["🧪🚀✨", "汉字かなカナ", "здравствуйте", "ελληνικά"])
    pad = _rand_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 16))
    variants.append((u + pad).encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # 9) IP/endpoint-like
    ep = rng.choice(["127.0.0.1:5000", "0.0.0.0:0", "[::1]:443", "[2001:db8::1]:65535", ":5000"])
    variants.append(ep.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    # 10) Path-like
    path = rng.choice([
        "/var/log/app.log",
        "/tmp/🔥/file.txt",
        "C:/Program Files/App/app.exe",
        "C:\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\etc\\hosts",
    ])
    variants.append(path.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00")

    return variants


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    variants = _make_variants(rng)

    # Concatenate multiple NUL-terminated strings so the fuzzer can choose any
    # substring up to NUL. Keep under MAX_TOTAL.
    buf = bytearray()
    rng.shuffle(variants)
    for v in variants:
        if len(buf) + len(v) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        buf.extend(v)

    # Ensure at least one NUL terminator at end for safety.
    if not buf or buf[-1] != 0:
        if len(buf) + 1 <= MAX_TOTAL:
            buf.append(0)
        else:
            # Replace last byte with NUL if we somehow filled exactly.
            buf[-1] = 0

    return bytes(buf)
